text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6).
test_case: Compare Annex 7 readings from 75 to 400 MHz with the log-increasing limit line of Appendix 6.
applies_because: The broadband limit applies to the LED drive electronics of the lamp.

text: When measured according to Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
test_case: Compare Annex 7 readings from 400 to 1,000 MHz with the 63 dBµV/m limit.
applies_because: The broadband limit applies to the LED drive electronics of the lamp.

text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7).
test_case: Compare Annex 8 readings from 75 to 400 MHz with the Appendix 7 limit line.
applies_because: The narrowband limit applies in case the lamp has an active electronic driver (oscillator above 9 kHz).

text: When measured according to Annex 8, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
test_case: Compare Annex 8 readings from 400 to 1,000 MHz with the 53 dBµV/m limit.
applies_because: The narrowband limit applies in case the lamp has an active electronic driver (oscillator above 9 kHz).

text: For an ESA for vehicles with 12 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a negative pulse amplitude of -100 V.
test_case: Record the maximum negative pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with -100 V.
applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 12 V supply.

text: For an ESA for vehicles with 24 V systems, the transient conducted emission on the supply lines shall not exceed a negative pulse amplitude of -450 V.
test_case: Record the maximum negative pulse amplitude per ISO 7637-2 and compare it with -450 V.
applies_because: Applies in case the lamp is designed for a 24 V supply.

text: The broadband emission limits apply to quasi-peak detection. If peak detectors are used to measure the rear lamp ESA, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied before comparing the readings with the limits.
test_case: Check that peak readings were corrected by 20 dB, or that quasi-peak detection was used, before comparison with the limits.
applies_because: The detector basis determines whether the lamp's measured emissions pass the limits.

text: For the rear lamp ESA, the maximum of the readings relative to the limit, over horizontal and vertical polarisation, in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
test_case: Review the test data to confirm that the worst-case polarisation reading in each band is used as the characteristic value and lies below the limit.
applies_because: This defines which reading of the lamp is assessed against the limit.

text: Narrowband emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be assessed with an average detector.
test_case: Verify in the test report that the narrowband emission results were measured with an average detector.
applies_because: The detector type defines which emission value the lamp electronics must keep below the narrowband limit.

text: In case the absorber chamber test is used, the ESA shall be exposed to antenna-generated radiation with the test field established by the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2 and with vertical polarization.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-2 absorber chamber test using vertical polarization and substitution-method field calibration.
applies_because: The absorber chamber is one of the permitted methods for showing the rear lamp's radiated immunity.

text: In case TEM cell testing is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to either the ESA or its wiring harness.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-3 TEM cell test in the maximum-coupling orientation chosen by the Technical Service.
applies_because: TEM cell testing is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

text: In case bulk current injection is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, either by the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA or by the closed loop method with the injection probe 900 mm from the ESA.
test_case: Perform ISO 11452-4 BCI on the lamp harness with the probe at 150 mm (substitution) or 900 mm (closed loop).
applies_because: BCI is a permitted method for covering the low-frequency part of the rear lamp's immunity range.

text: As an alternative to bench BCI, the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the injection probe 150 mm from the ESA.
test_case: If chosen, perform in-vehicle BCI per ISO 11451-4 with the probe 150 mm from the lamp.
applies_because: This is a permitted alternative for demonstrating the rear lamp's BCI immunity.

text: In case stripline testing is used, the ESA wiring harness shall be subjected to the specified field strengths according to ISO 11452-5.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-5 stripline test on the lamp harness.
applies_because: Stripline testing is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

text: In case the reverberation chamber test is used, the ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-11 using a test setup with ground plane, unless otherwise specified.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-11 reverberation chamber test with a ground-plane setup.
applies_because: The reverberation chamber is a permitted method for the rear lamp ESA.

text: Each lamp function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.
test_case: Review the type-approval test report covering all paragraph 4 and 5 checks for each function.
applies_because: The rear combination lamp is submitted for R148 approval for its R, S and AR functions.
drop_reason: Pure announcement that other paragraphs apply

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 4.
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at HV, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the geometric visibility angles, compared against Table 4.
applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp of category R1 or R2.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 7.
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at HV, across the Figure A3-I grid and within the geometric visibility angles, compared against Table 7.
applies_because: The product includes a stop lamp of category S1 or S2.

text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 10.
test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples over the Figure A3-V grid, compared against Table 10.
applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp of category AR.

text: The light emitted by production lamps shall comply with the required chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production samples per paragraph 4.9 with a spectroradiometer and check them against the red and white colour boundaries.
applies_because: Conformity of production covers the colorimetric characteristics of each lamp function.

text: For a production retro-reflector chosen at random, no measured photometric value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
test_case: Measure the RI values of random production samples and compare them with 80 % of the Table 3 minima.
applies_because: This is the photometric deviation limit for production retro-reflectors, referenced by 3.5.1.1.
drop_reason: Duplicate of C-0282 (same CoP photometric tolerance, Annex 2 1.2).

text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for trailer retro-reflectors when observed from a distance of 10 m.
test_case: Visually inspect the illuminating surface from 10 m to confirm it is not mistakable for a triangle.
applies_because: P-05 is a non-triangular Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector.

text: The retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. It shall also withstand a repeat with the device turned through 180° (rear face covered by about 20 mm of water), followed immediately by immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
test_case: Immerse the lamp/retro-reflector in 50 °C water in normal and inverted positions, then in 25 °C water.
applies_because: P-05 is a retro-reflector within the lamp and is subject to the water penetration test.

text: After the water penetration test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; visible presence of water means failure.
test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting surface for water; in case of doubt, re-measure the RI per 5.1.3.2.2.
applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for P-05 (Class IA, and Class IB unless the alternative applies).

text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the illuminating surface area to be used for photometric measurement of the retro-reflector.
test_case: Check the approval documentation for the declared perimeter of the illuminating surface.
applies_because: The design documentation of P-05 must define the measured area.
drop_reason: Obligation on the manufacturer to specify the perimeter.

text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than those of Table 3, in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI measurement per Annex 4 Part 1 and compare with Table 3.
applies_because: P-05 is a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", its RI at β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and a divergence of 20', measured in the rotational position about the axis of reference giving minimum RI, shall conform to paragraph 5. The device may be rotated ±5° from that position if the specified values for the other angles are not attained.
test_case: Rotate the sample about its reference axis to the minimum-RI position and measure the RI at all required angles.
applies_because: P-05 may not carry a TOP marking, so its orientation-dependent RI must still comply.
drop_reason: Duplicate of C-0289 and C-0290 (same paragraph, Annex 4 Part 1 1.2).

text: Production retro-reflectors shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates for red.
test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of randomly selected production retro-reflectors and verify they lie within the red boundaries of the Regulation.
applies_because: The red retro-reflector must keep its colour within the red limits in series production.

text: The retro-reflection (RI) of the retro-reflector shall be assessed with the device illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
test_case: Verify that the photometric test report states Illuminant A source conditions for all RI measurements of the retro-reflector.
applies_because: This defines the illuminant under which the red retro-reflector must achieve its RI values.

text: In case of Class IB (lamp not watertight) where the moisture and dust tests are applied as the alternative to the water penetration test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open during the water spray test, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
test_case: Inspect the test sample to confirm drain holes and openings are unobstructed and drain wicks are fitted as in production.
applies_because: The retro-reflector may be Class IB in a non-watertight rear lamp, and the moisture test is then an option for it.
drop_reason: Test set-up detail (openings and drain wicks during the test).

text: In case of Class IB with the dust test applied, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open during the dust exposure, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
test_case: Inspect the sample before dust exposure to confirm openings are open and wicks are installed.
applies_because: The dust test is the companion test to the moisture alternative for a Class IB retro-reflector.
drop_reason: Test set-up detail for the dust test.

text: After a recovery period of 48 hours following the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, measured as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6 at an entrance angle β2 = 5° and an observation angle α = 20', shall be not less than the minimum value of the referenced Table 9 and not more than the maximum value of the referenced Table 10.
test_case: After 48 h recovery and removal of salt deposits, measure RA at β2 = 5° and α = 20' and compare the result with the referenced limits.
applies_because: This photometric pass criterion after the corrosion test applies to the retro-reflective areas of the device under test.
drop_reason: RA coefficient tables apply to retro-reflective marking materials, not to Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and on a flat, horizontal surface, in normal condition of use.
test_case: Measure height and orientation with the vehicle unladen on a flat horizontal surface.
applies_because: This defines the vehicle condition in which the lamp's height and orientation must comply.
drop_reason: Describes the verification conditions (unladen vehicle, flat surface), i.e. test method.

text: The maximum height above the ground of each rear lamp function shall be measured from the highest point, and the minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
test_case: Measure the highest and lowest points of each function's apparent surface above the ground.
applies_because: This defines how the height limits of the lamp functions are assessed.
drop_reason: Measurement convention for height, i.e. method.

text: For the purpose of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the height of the rear lamp above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
test_case: Measure the H-plane height of the installed lamp.
applies_because: Reduced vertical visibility angles may apply to low-mounted rear functions.

text: The width position of each rear lamp function shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface furthest from the median longitudinal plane for the overall-width distance, and from the inner edges of the apparent surfaces for the distance between lamps.
test_case: Measure the outer and inner edges of the apparent surfaces relative to the vehicle centreline and outer edge.
applies_because: This defines how the lateral position requirements of the functions are assessed.

text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of any red function of the rear lamp for an observer moving within Zone 1 (between 1 m and 2.2 m height, bounded by planes at 15° outwards) in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle.
test_case: Perform an observation or CAD sight-line check from Zone 1, 25 m in front of the vehicle.
applies_because: The lamp contains red rear functions.

text: Zone 1, within which the red apparent surfaces shall not be directly visible towards the front, is bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. In width it is bounded by a vertical plane forming an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane. That plane passes through the point of contact of a vertical plane parallel to the median longitudinal plane that delimits the vehicle's overall width; where there are several points of contact, the foremost point applies.
test_case: Lay out Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle using the 1 m and 2.2 m height limits and the 15° outward width limits, then verify the lamp is not visible from anywhere within it.
applies_because: This zone defines the observation region in which the red rear lamp's front-visibility check is made.

text: In case of doubt, the requirement of no direct visibility of red light towards the front shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp. This intensity is as verified during type approval of the lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body where applicable.
test_case: Measure, or take from the lamp type-approval report, the red luminous intensity emitted towards the front, including any influence of the vehicle body, and confirm it is ≤ 0.25 cd per lamp.
applies_because: This relaxation allows the red rear lamp to demonstrate front-visibility compliance by meeting a forward luminous intensity limit.
